query_snapshot: What two temperature-related material-selection concerns does NASA SP-8119 identify for cryogenic disconnects?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- Some seal materials used in disconnects (for example, Teflon and certain plastics) become very brittle at cryogenic temperatures and can fracture or otherwise fail (fracture before obtaining adequate support; cold flow and installation/handling problems are noted), so their use in cryogenic disconnect seals is limited or must be treated cautiously. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 65-66, chunk af0b8a8f; nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 69-70, chunk 214c6dfc]
- Widely different coefficients of thermal expansion/contraction among materials can cause large bolting problems, improper clearances or fits, loss of preload, flange deflection/warpage, and seal leakage in disconnects; SP-8119 therefore recommends using materials with similar coefficients of expansion or accounting for thermal contraction in design. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 85-88, chunk 91eb9fc5; nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 12-13, chunk 1bd93be2]
